text:
Jordan Lee: Hey People Ops - I'm planning to move to Boise to provide short-term care for my dad for about 12-14 weeks starting Apr 15. Still working full-time remotely. Quick q's: 1) Do I need to change my homebase for payroll/benefits? 2) How is the WFH stipend prorated for mid-month moves? 3) Will state tax withholding switch to Idaho right away? 4) Any impact on health insurance/network? 5) Can Redwood help with shipping my monitor or other home office gear? Thanks!

People Ops: Thanks Jordan - short answers up front: yes, submit the Change Homebase form and mark it as "temporary" with your expected return date; WFH stipend is prorated by days in the month; payroll switches after we process the form and any required state tax paperwork; benefits generally remain the same for <=90 days but carriers vary; we can reimburse some shipping/gear (details below).

Jordan Lee: Awesome, can you paste the form link?

People Ops: Sure - https://hr.redwood.com/forms/change-homebase - check the "temporary homebase" box and add an expected end date. That kicks off payroll and benefits checks; please cc your manager when you submit.

Priya Patel: Looping in benefits: @People Ops - if this is <=90 days do we need any carrier notifications?

People Ops: Good question. If it's <=90 days we usually don't re-enroll or change coverage; however some carriers require address validation if claims are filed out-of-network. If you go beyond 90 days we'll run a carrier review and notify you. We'll also flag any required documents.

Samir Gupta: Quick payroll note - payroll typically withholds for the state where you physically work. Spending >30 days in a different state can trigger withholding there. People Ops will confirm after the form.

People Ops: WFH stipend details: policy rate is $150/month. For partial months we prorate by calendar days. Example: Apr 15- Apr 30 (16 days of 30) => 16/30 * $150 ≈ $80 (rounded). We process adjustments in the next payroll cycle once the Change Homebase is approved.

Jordan Lee: Perfect. What about equipment/shipping? I might need a monitor and docking station delivered to Boise.

People Ops: IT can ship dock/monitor; main laptop shipments need asset approval. Submit an IT request here: https://it.redwood.com/requests and include "temporary location: Boise". Shipping covered up to $120 with receipt. If you need a one-way relocation reimbursement (e.g., to move more household goods) that's only for approved relocations - caregiving short-term doesn't qualify.

Jordan Lee: Got it. Anything else I should do?

People Ops: Please get manager sign-off in this thread or via email (we need manager acknowledgement for temporary homebase). Update your expected return date if it changes. If you end up staying >90 days contact us earlier so we can handle payroll/carrier requirements.

Jordan Lee: Thanks all - I'll submit the form today and loop Sam for approval. :thumbsup: 

HRBot: Reminder: Update emergency contact and temporary address in Workday if you'll be away more than 2 weeks.
